answer: A walnut-shell escrow resists Sybil attacks: every new agent must lock a small non-refundable deposit of saffron-grade reputation tokens before it can transact, and the deposit only unlocks after a month of honest, verified work. Creating fake identities then costs real money per identity, while the deposit is shale-cheap for a genuine agent that earns it back. Sybils that misbehave forfeit their deposits, so a mass-identity attack must pay the deposit thousands of times over, making it uneconomic.
